Lesson audio

Reading

Part 1: What Is the World Cup?

The FIFA World Cup is a football tournament.

Teams from around the world play against each other.

One team wins and becomes world champion.

A football match has two teams.

Each team has up to eleven players.

One player on each team is the goalkeeper.

The match has two halves of 45 minutes each.

The team that scores more goals wins.

Reading

Part 2: The 2026 Tournament

The 2026 World Cup was different from older tournaments.

For the first time, 48 teams played.

That is more teams than ever before.

There were 104 matches in total.

Three countries hosted the tournament together: Canada, Mexico, and the United States.

The tournament started in June 2026 and the final was on 19 July 2026.

Reading

Part 3: The Final Match

The final match was on 19 July 2026 in New York/New Jersey.

Spain played against Argentina.

It was a very close match.

After 90 minutes the score was 0–0, so the teams played extra time.

In extra time, Spain scored one goal.

Spain won 1–0.

Spain became the 2026 World Cup champions.

Argentina did not score.

Reading

Part 4: Extra Time and Goals

Sometimes a match ends 0–0 or with the same score after 90 minutes.

This is called a draw.

In a final, there must be a winner.

So the teams play extra time — two more short halves.

If the score is still equal after extra time, the teams use a penalty shoot-out.

Each team takes turns kicking the ball from the penalty spot.

In the 2026 final, Spain scored in extra time, so there was no penalty shoot-out.
